title: What did Java 21 add overall, and why is Java 21 a common upgrade target (LTS)?
keyPoints: Java 21 is a Long-Term Support release, the primary enterprise upgrade target after Java 17
Virtual threads (JEP 444) enable cheap blocking concurrency with millions of lightweight threads
Pattern matching for switch (JEP 441) supports type patterns, guards, and exhaustiveness checking
Record patterns (JEP 440) deconstruct records directly in instanceof and switch expressions
Sequenced collections (JEP 431) add getFirst(), getLast(), and reversed() to List, Set, and Map views
Generational ZGC (JEP 439) delivers sub-millisecond GC pauses with generational collection
String templates and unnamed patterns were introduced as previews

s1_definition.oneliner: Java 21 is an LTS release that finalizes virtual threads, pattern matching for switch, record patterns, sequenced collections, and generational ZGC.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **LTS** – Long-Term Support release, supported for years with security patches; enterprises upgrade LTS to LTS (8 to 11 to 17 to 21).
- **Virtual threads (JEP 444)** – lightweight, JVM-managed threads for I/O-bound concurrency, replacing the need for reactive frameworks.
- **Pattern matching for switch (JEP 441)** – switch cases can match types, apply guards, and the compiler enforces exhaustiveness over sealed types.
- **Record patterns (JEP 440)** – deconstruct records in `instanceof` and `switch` to bind components directly.
- **Sequenced collections (JEP 431)** – `getFirst()`, `getLast()`, `addFirst()`, `reversed()` added to ordered collection interfaces.
- **Generational ZGC (JEP 439)** – low-latency garbage collector with generational separation for improved throughput.
s1_definition.analogy: Java 21 is the bank's major renovation year. Virtual threads are unlimited cheap clerks. Pattern matching switch is smarter routing at the service counter. Record patterns let you unpack customer forms inline. Sequenced collections give easy first-and-last access to queues. Generational ZGC is a faster waste management system that collects small trash frequently and big trash rarely.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Java 21 is the most significant LTS release since Java 8. It brings virtual threads for scalable I/O-bound concurrency, pattern matching for switch with exhaustiveness checking, record patterns for inline deconstruction, sequenced collections for first-and-last access, and generational ZGC for sub-millisecond garbage collection pauses.

The combination of records, sealed classes, and pattern matching gives Java algebraic-data-type modeling for the first time. You define a sealed hierarchy of records, then use an exhaustive switch to handle each variant. Adding a new record without updating the switch is a compile error. This eliminates an entire class of bugs that the visitor pattern was previously needed to prevent.

Enterprises adopt Java 21 because it is LTS (years of security patches and vendor support), Spring Boot 3.2+ fully supports it, and the productivity gains from virtual threads alone justify the upgrade. Teams that previously invested in reactive programming (Project Reactor, RxJava) can now write simple blocking code that scales equally well.

Remember one sentence: Java 21 LTS finalizes virtual threads, pattern matching switch, record patterns, sequenced collections, and generational ZGC as the enterprise baseline.
